newsitem.title: UK: Oil steadies as traders digest $2 slump.
newsitem.headline: Oil steadies as traders digest $2 slump.

text.p: Oil prices steadied on Monday, stemming a slide which knocked nearly $2 from the price of crude in the space of a week.
London March futures for bellwether North Sea Brent Blend at 1602 GMT were trading up 11 cents at $22.65 a barrel.

Milder weather in Europe and the United States and a steady recovery of lean heating oil stocks on both sides of the Atlantic has pulled prices down from the six-year highs reached earlier in this winter.
Suffering a hangover from last week's sharp losses, Brent again opened weaker on Monday morning, trading as low as $22.29 before staging a modest recovery.
"The market seems to be consolidating at these levels but it's still very volatile," said a trader in London.
Declining demand for crude to feed refineries in the United States and Europe ahead of spring maintenance closures was also beginning to make its impact felt on the market, traders said.
But while demand for heating oil has not been as strong as expected, inventories still remain tight enough to discourage any immediate further price fall, dealers said.
U.S. distillates stocks (which including heating oil) last week stood at 126 million barrels compared to 143.5 million the same time a year ago.
Deteriorating oil refining margins were choking demand for crude as refiners in Asia reduced throughput at some plants.

"Refiners are now experiencing very negative margins," said a Singapore trader. "Although margins only turned bad very recently, there is talk about cutting runs as the outlook does not look too bright.
Dealers said Chinese demand had been covered ahead of the lunar New Year while heating oil demand had passed its peak in north Asia.
Newly-commissioned South Korean refineries, designed to meet growing domestic needs, were looking to export some oil products.
